You're joining an ongoing research project in /home/sprite/github-gigs (a git repo with existing commits — read SUMMARY.md, DEEP_REVIEW.md, FINAL_VERDICT.md first for context, plus README of the original inspiration: the referenced GitHub issue is https://github.com/team113/messenger/issues/382, titled "[$400] Display local and push notifications with avatars" — team113/messenger is now archived).

## Background
The user's original discovery, team113/messenger, was NOT on any third-party bounty platform (not Algora, not Polar.sh, not IssueHunt, not Bountysource) — it used its own fully manual, in-house convention: issue titles prefixed with a literal price tag like `[$400]`, combined with a custom GitHub label named "help wanted" whose label DESCRIPTION explicitly read "This issue is looking for freelancer to work on it". No bot, no external platform, no dashboard — just a human maintainer manually managing payment via a plain GitHub convention. This is structurally invisible to any bounty-aggregator platform (Algora/Polar/etc.) since there's no integration to scrape — the ONLY way to find more of these is raw GitHub search across issue titles/bodies/labels.

Two other teammates are in parallel hunting Algora and Polar.sh specifically — your job is different: find MORE small/medium real, currently-active open-source projects that manage bounties themselves via a custom convention like team113 did, not tied to any third-party platform.

Known false-positive traps from earlier rounds (avoid repeating, read DEEP_REVIEW.md and ROUND3_ALGORA_HUNT.md for full detail):
- Projects paying in their own near-worthless custom token (e.g. FreezingMoon/AncientBeast pays "XTR" — a dead MintMe-issued token with ~$0 liquidity) — always check if the currency symbol is a REAL fiat/major-crypto (`$`, `USD`, `EUR`, well-known ticker with real market cap) vs. a project-invented token.
- Fake/test "bounty sandbox" repos benchmarking AI coding agents (red flags: <50 stars claiming large bounties, labels like "Autonomous/Autonomus Agents Only", repo description admitting "sandbox fixture", dead single-day commit history, dozens of wildly generic auto-generated-sounding issue titles like "Add X guard/module/assistant").
- Historical/dead programs (last bounty closed years ago, e.g. RudderStack/openScale/Etherpad/celo-org's old Gitcoin-era bounties were all found dead).
- district0x-style false positives where "bounty" is just a word mentioned in an unrelated document, not an actual paid task.

## Your task
Use GitHub's Search API creatively to find custom-convention bounty projects. Ideas to try (GitHub's search silently strips `$` and other punctuation from free-text queries, so searching literally for `[$` doesn't work well — work around this):
- `label:"help wanted" state:closed` combined with a plausible currency word like `usd` `paid` `reward` `compensat` in:body, then manually inspect title text client-side for a `$NUMBER` pattern using your own reading/regex rather than relying on GitHub's tokenization.
- Search issue titles for the literal word patterns that survive tokenization even without `$`, like `BOUNTY` (all caps) combined with `state:closed` (a repo that has CLOSED priced issues over time = real track record) then check if currently anything is open too.
- Try label names beyond "help wanted"/"bounty": some projects use "paid", "sponsored", "funded", "compensation", "freelance".
- Try issue body phrase searches copying team113's exact label description convention: `"looking for freelancer" in:body`, `"freelancer to work on" in:body` (round 2 already tried these once and got 29 hits each but didn't deep-verify any — worth revisiting and actually vetting a few properly this time).
- Consider niche/gaming communities (SS13 forks, similar to the SPLURT-Station find from earlier rounds, which DID confirm real $ amounts) — search for more forks of that ecosystem or similar volunteer-driven-but-funded game projects.

## Verification checklist (mandatory per candidate)
1. `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}` — check stars, pushed_at (want recent, ideally within ~2 months), archived==false.
2. Confirm the currency is REAL money (fiat symbol or well-known major cryptocurrency with actual market cap/liquidity — if unsure, note it as "unverified currency" rather than assuming).
3. Confirm there's at least one issue CLOSED under this convention with real signs of resolution (merged PR, or a maintainer comment) — proof it's not just an aspirational label nobody acts on.
4. Check currently OPEN priced issues: is there an assignee already? How many comments/competing attempts? Prefer low-comment, unassigned, recently-posted ones.

## Rate limits
Unauthenticated GitHub API: 60 core requests/hour, 10 search requests/min. Pace search calls ~7s apart, core calls ~2-3s apart. Check `curl -s https://api.github.com/rate_limit` if unsure.

## Output
Write findings to a NEW file: /home/sprite/github-gigs/manual_convention_hunt_findings.md. List any genuinely good candidates (repo/issue URLs, amounts, currency verification, competition assessment, health stats). Be honest if nothing new turns up beyond what's already documented (Expensify and SPLURT-Station SS13 are already known — only report those again if you find NEW specific currently-open issues in them worth flagging).

Do NOT run git commands. Do NOT modify/delete existing files. Do NOT spawn further subagents.

Reply with a concise summary (under 300 words) when done: how many new genuine candidates you found, and the single best one if any.

# Итог: поиск GitHub-проектов с оплатой за issues

Твоя теория подтвердилась — таких проектов реально несколько десятков, просто нет
единого каталога, и большинство людей их не ищут через GitHub Search (хотя
`label:bounty` — это встроенная кросс-репозиторная фича GitHub, которой почти
никто не пользуется).

Полные сырые данные: `results.json` (298 репо, 111 репо с issues), красивая
таблица: `REPORT.md`. Скрипты: `scan_github_bounties.py` (поиск) +
`build_report.py` (отчёт) — можно перезапускать когда угодно.

## 1. Уже существующий курируемый список (для référence)

**kunovsky/paid-open-source-projects** — репозиторий-список именно того, что ты
описал. team113/messenger там НЕТ, что подтверждает: такие списки неполные и
полагаться только на них нельзя.

| Проект | Оплата | Как |
|---|---|---|
| RudderStack | $2000/баунти | github.com/rudderlabs/rudder-server |
| Expensify | $250-500/баунти | github.com/Expensify/App |
| BusKill | $2340 | github.com/BusKill/buskill-app |
| tscircuit | $5-300 (через Algora) | algora.io/tscircuit/bounties |
| Trigger.dev | $50-200 | github.com/triggerdotdev/trigger.dev |
| AppFlowy | $500/мес (mentorship) | appflowy.io |

## 2. Найдено "с нуля" через сырой поиск (не в списках) — похоже на реальные

Это самое близкое к твоему кейсу с team113 — маленькие/средние проекты со своей
доморощенной конвенцией "лейбл + цена в issue", без сторонней платформы:

- **Expensify/App** — `[$250] VES currency is incorrectly converted to USD` — подтверждает данные из списка выше, но это отдельная живая issue, не из списка.
- **aeternity/aepp-token-migration-backend-nodejs** — `[bounty] migrate Go backend to Node.js (CHF 800)`
- **evilew/gs13-outdated** — `[BUG-FIXING BOUNTY - 50 USD] Weapon jamming bug`
- **lnbits/lnbits** — `BOUNTY 800k sat` (~ на момент публикации сотни $) на фиче
- **nebulouslabs/sia** — `Bounty for Duplicati Integration: 400,000 SC` (Siacoin)
- **celo-org/celo-monorepo** — `[Bounty] CeloCLI Staking Rewards should show whole Wei`
- **freezingmoon/ancientbeast** — `[bounty: 22 XTR]` (открытая инди-игра)
- **unitystation/unitystation** — `Bug Discovery Bounty` (открытый форк SS13 на Unity)
- **splurt-station/s.p.l.u.r.t-station-13** и **-tg** — несколько `[BOUNTY]`-issues (форки SS13, активное сообщество)
- **district0x/district-proposals** — ссылается на отдельную платформу **Bounty0x.io**, которую я раньше не проверял
- **bigchaindb/*** (4 репозитория) — исторически платили через Gitcoin
- **boundlessfi/bounties** — отдельный репозиторий-баунти-борд у живого проекта
- **warpspeedopen-source/warpspeed-bounties** — маленький (1 star, 1 автор), явно ранняя стадия, статус неясен — issues без откликов, но заявлен как "Paid open-source bounty tasks"

Рекомендую проверять каждый вручную перед тем как тратить время: смотреть, реально
ли платят (история закрытых issues + комментарии мейнтейнера о выплате), как
у team113 было видно по `[$400]` в заголовке и реальной истории закрытых issues.

## 3. ⚠️ Важная находка: похоже на ферму фейковых баунти

Заметил кластер репозиториев с абсолютно одинаковым форматом
`[$XX BOUNTY] [Язык] <generic-задача>` и лейблами `help wanted, good first issue,
bounty, language:X`:

`123a-bcd/nailstorm-bounty-forge-358`, `123a-bcd/zeroeye`, `9904099/zeroeye`,
`0106hyh/kickama-manifest-wizard`, `xxnjms1-code/kickama-prize-lab`,
`2lll5/tentoftrials`, `saiaaax/cyberninja-dojo`

Проверил один детально (`123a-bcd/nailstorm-bounty-forge-358`, issue #1):
- Репозиторий создан 17 июня 2026 (**2 недели назад**), 0 звёзд, описание
  ("Trading and market platform") никак не связано с содержанием issue
  (rate-limiting в benchmark-тулзе).
- Аккаунт **`Rachaelisa`** оставил **6 одинаковых спам-комментариев** "/attempt #1..."
  за 16 минут — явно бот.
- Аккаунт **`Nexussyn`** сразу прислал крипто-адрес (USDC) и попросил перевести
  деньги, не сделав ни строчки кода — классический скам-паттерн.
- Один из "решателей" на этом issue (`9904099`) — это одновременно **владелец
  другого репозитория из этого же кластера** (`9904099/zeroeye`) — то есть один и
  тот же оператор одновременно "заказчик" в одном репо и "исполнитель" в другом.
- Есть и комментарий с явно AI-сгенерированным решением на китайском ("AI生成的解决方案").

Вывод: это, вероятнее всего, **не настоящие рабочие места**, а тестовый полигон
для автономных AI-агентов/ботов (или скам-сеть, собирающая крипто-адреса под
видом "оплаты баунти"). **Не советую туда лезть** и тратить время — включил их в
`REPORT.md` только для полноты картины, но явно помечаю как подозрительные.

## 4. Инструменты на будущее (без написания кода)

- **algora.io/bounties** — крупнейшая живая площадка именно "оплата за GitHub issue"
  на сегодня (2026), с публичным лидербордом. У них закрытый API у меня не
  получилось стабильно вытащить (то ли поменяли схему, то ли ограничили доступ
  без org) — но страницу можно смотреть глазами.
- **github.com/issues?q=is:open+is:issue+label:bounty** — встроенный кросс-репо
  поиск GitHub, который мало кто использует (тот самый секрет команды team113).
- Мой скрипт `scan_github_bounties.py` можно перезапускать периодически (раз в
  неделю/месяц) — он ищет по 13 паттернам (readme-упоминания Algora/IssueHunt/
  BountySource, topics, лейблы issues) и сохраняет всё в `results.json`.

body: Just documenting it here for awareness. I spun up a Rocky Linux 9 container last night, and was able to get the out-of-the-box configuration building with the llvm-toolset (clang-18) package. I had to install a handful of dependencies, but they were all available in the standard repositories. Given that Rocky is intended to mirror Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), that does bode well for tt-metal being able to build on RHEL9.

Edit: The new sub-dependency libisl.so.23 (which was hooked today) is not available in any of the Rocky/Fedora repos, which is stuck on v0.16. So any Rocky builds going forward are going to need to build libisl. See #21635 for more information.

Edit2: A recent update added support for OpenMPI. I haven't tested this on the rocky container (yet), but on fedora, the openMPI/-devel packages put everything under `/usr/lib64/openmpi` with subdirectories `bin lib include share`. This appears to be because redhat ships both openmpi as well as the alternate implementation `mpich`. The FindOpenMPI.cmake that ships with the cmake-data package doesn't seem to find it by default (I probably need to put in a ticket with RH), so the workaround was to add `/usr/lib64/openmpi/bin` etc to their respective PATH environment variables. Just documenting this here since its the same distro provider.

body: Just documenting it here for awareness. I spun up a Rocky Linux 9 container last night, and was able to get the out-of-the-box configuration building with the llvm-toolset (clang-18) package. I had to install a handful of dependencies, but they were all available in the standard repositories. Given that Rocky is intended to mirror Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), that does bode well for tt-metal being able to build on RHEL9.

Edit: The new sub-dependency libisl.so.23 (which was hooked today) is not available in any of the Rocky/Fedora repos, which is stuck on v0.16. So any Rocky builds going forward are going to need to build libisl. See #21635 for more information.

Edit2: A recent update added support for OpenMPI. I haven't tested this on the rocky container (yet), but on fedora, the openMPI/-devel packages put everything under `/usr/lib64/openmpi` with subdirectories `bin lib include share`. This appears to be because redhat ships both openmpi as well as the alternate implementation `mpich`. The FindOpenMPI.cmake that ships with the cmake-data package doesn't seem to find it by default (I probably need to put in a ticket with RH), so the workaround was to add `/usr/lib64/openmpi/bin` etc to their respective PATH environment variables. Just documenting this here since its the same distro provider.

# Background

Polls have two purposes:
1. Quick and easy single selection polls to quickly gather thoughts
2. Ranked choice polls that help to collect detailed feedback. 


We want to be able to support both needs, as detailed below.

# User Stories

## Megan - Group DM Member (simple poll)

Megan is in a group chat with her friends. She wants to be able to quickly ask folks which dress of hers looks best. To do so, she creates a poll. In the poll creation menu, she is able to to upload images and write text next next to them. She is able to set a title and a duration. She also gets to toggle ranked voting and anonymous responses. Finally, she has the option to allow people to select custom responses. 

In this case, she creates a simple poll with no ranked voting and no custom responses. Once Megan hits confirm, a poll appears in the chat. 

### Desktop
On desktop, Megan's friends see a poll appear with each (smaller) image / text option. The header has the title and Megan's profile picture. 

The results are hidden from them until they hit submit. Clicking on each image brings it up bigger with the text as a caption. Users are able to click left or right arrows or use their arrow keys to go between options. Double clicking on the image selects it as the selected choice. They are able to undo that choice by double clicking again.

# Manual-convention bounty hunt (round: raw GitHub Search, non-platform)

Scope: find MORE projects that manage bounties themselves via a custom
GitHub convention (price in issue title + label), like team113/messenger's
`[$400]` + "help wanted" label — explicitly NOT Algora/Polar/IssueHunt/
Bountysource (other teammates cover those). Search API only, ~14 search
calls + ~15 core calls used, paced within rate limits.

## Method notes (what worked / didn't)

- `label:"help wanted" state:closed` + currency words, and the exact
  team113-style phrases `"looking for freelancer" in:body` /
  `"freelancer to work on" in:body` (re-tried from round 2) — **both are
  dead ends**. 100% noise: Upwork/job-board postings, "hire me" spam,
  generic freelance marketplaces. Zero real project-bounty hits in ~110
  results inspected. Do not re-run these again in future rounds.
- Label sweep `label:paid` / `label:sponsored` / `label:funded` /
  `label:compensation` / `label:freelance` — mostly false positives
  (generic product labels, unrelated "sponsored" tracking labels,
  scientific/software terms). One real hit surfaced: `warpspeedopen-source/
  warpspeed-bounties` (already known/dead from round 1, still just 1
  star, no visible activity — skip again).
- **What actually worked well:** literal `bounty` / `BOUNTY` / `[Bounty:`
  in `in:title`, `is:open`/`is:closed`, sorted by created date descending.
  This surfaces real projects reliably once you filter out the AI-agent
  bounty-farm clusters (very recognizable now: generic titles like "Add
  X guard/helper/utility", `xevrion-v2/agent-playground`, `auscaster/
  frantic-board`, `ritesh-1918/HELPDESK.AI`, `zhangjiayang6835-cyber/
  ai-research`, `dwebagents/AgentPipe`, `9904099`/`123a-bcd` clusters from
  earlier rounds — all still there, all still fake/farm/honeypot).
- New false-positive pattern this round: **"bot-detection honeypot"
  bounties** — trivial tasks explicitly titled to test whether AI agents

Three genuinely real, currently-active, non-platform manual bounty
conventions found this round, none of them previously documented:
**tenstorrent** (tt-metal/tt-blacksmith), **TauCetiStation/TauCetiClassic**,

(new bounties get assigned within days), rather than continuing broad
GitHub-wide keyword sweeps — the keyword-sweep approach is now heavily
saturated with AI-agent bounty-farm noise and returns diminishing real
hits per search.
